## Final Response

# 1. Main Body
As autonomous artificial intelligence agents expand across software engineering, physical robotics, and enterprise infrastructure, emerging empirical data reveals critical operational bottlenecks and security risks.
In enterprise security, Microsoft introduced Guardian Agents under Project Perception to monitor unpredictable agent behavior, warning that deployed agents effectively act as internal insider threats [1].
To isolate agent activity and mitigate untrusted frontier model actions, Microsoft integrated Defender agent detection and joined Nvidia's Open Agent Safety Platform [1].
Furthermore, Microsoft's CEO Satya Nadella emphasized the necessity of separating the supply of intelligence from organizational authority over it [1].
Addressing financial risk in non-deterministic large language models, American Express unveiled its Intent Intelligence Framework to prevent unauthorized agent purchases [2].
The Amex framework utilizes a Create Intent API, an Intent ID, and a Proof of Intent Token to bind user constraints before issuing secure payment credentials at checkout [2].
This framework complements Amex's ACE Developer Toolkit to capture user intent early in transaction flows and streamline dispute resolution [2].
Despite corporate enthusiasm for agentic commerce, consumer adoption of external third-party ordering tools remains extremely sparse [3].
DoorDash reported that external AI agents utilizing its Model Context Protocol connector generated only several hundred food delivery orders in Q3 2026 [3].
In contrast, DoorDash's internal Ask DoorDash feature accelerated shopping cart creation fivefold and increased basket values by nearly 50% [3].
In software development, empirical analysis of over 700 firms by Harvard researchers demonstrated that AI coding agents do not increase net software output [4].
While AI agents increased raw lines of code by 30%, commits by 20%, and pull requests by 23%, downstream code review bottlenecks absorbed these gains [4].
Average pull request review times increased by 49%, and requested revisions nearly doubled, requiring a 14% increase in human review staff [4].
Automated agents have also introduced external disruption by generating unsolicited spam slop across social media platforms [5].
Startup iLands deployed autonomous agents like Ren and Aria to register accounts on Mastodon, X, and Bluesky, prompting server blocks and FTC spam complaints [5].
Internal enterprise deployment initiatives have similarly encountered severe friction due to technical instability [6].
Meta's internal Project OT aimed to slash team headcounts by up to 60% and establish an AI-native organization using agent-assisted management [6].
However, Meta scrapped the plan after AI agents caused a 40% increase in major technical and security incidents and a 70% increase in resolution time [6].
Meta CTO Andrew Bosworth noted that while infrastructure code changes surged 220%, user-facing feature improvements increased by only 36% [6].
Conversely, specialized frameworks demonstrate significant success when applying AI agents to physical automation [7].
Nvidia GEAR lab, alongside CMU and UC Berkeley researchers, developed ENPIRE, an agentic harness that enables AI coding agents to autonomously direct robot training [7].
Utilizing multi-agent teams of up to eight agents, ENPIRE achieved a 99% success rate across complex robotic manipulation tasks including zip tie cutting and GPU motherboard installation [7].
The ENPIRE framework automates policy refinement and failure analysis, surpassing human-in-the-loop benchmarks while incurring substantial token consumption costs [7].
